title: Pilot Surge Capacity & SLO Burn Model
body:
Purpose:
This sheet models short-run "surge" pilots for new feature rollouts across Dedicated and Hosted tiers. It helps the product-ops and SRE teams plan capacity, estimate SLO burn for each cohort, and define automatic fallback thresholds. Use during pilot approvals, traffic ramp decisions, and canary-to-production transitions.

How to use (quick):
- Fill the Pilot Inputs section (start date, target cohort size, target qps per user, model variant).
- Choose the Deployment Mode: hosted | dedicated | private.
- Review 'Projected Supply' vs 'Projected Demand' to see capacity shortfalls at 15/30/60/90 minute horizons.
- Check the 'SLO Burn' column; if projected burn > allowed threshold, trigger the contingency checklist.

Sheet layout (tabs represented as sections in this doc):
1) Pilot Inputs (cells A1..F20)
   - Pilot name: string
   - Start date: date
   - Cohort ID: string/JIRA ticket
   - Expected MAU (cohort): number
   - Expected peak concurrency per user: decimal
   - Avg tokens per request: number
   - Model variant: e.g. redwood-2.1-8bit
   - Deployment mode: hosted/dedicated/private

2) Traffic Phases (A22..G50)
   Columns: Phase name | Relative traffic % | Duration (mins) | Ramp type (linear/step) | Notes | Owner | Linked runbook
   Example rows:
   Phase 1 | 5% | 60 | linear | smoke + telemetry validation | eng-release | PRODOPS-452
   Phase 2 | 20% | 180 | step | soft-launch internal | eng-release | confluence.redwood/display/PDX/Pilot+Surge+Runbook

3) Capacity & Supply Model (A52..L120)
   Columns: Region | Pool type | GPUs | Avg tokens/sec per GPU | Measured latency p50/p95 | Capacity tokens/min | Headroom% | Notes
   Sample formulas (explicit cells):
   - Capacity tokens/min = GPUs * avg_tokens_per_sec_per_GPU * 60
   - Headroom% = (Capacity tokens/min - Projected tokens/min)/Capacity tokens/min
   - If Headroom% < 0.12 then "low" else if <0.25 then "tight" else "healthy"

   Example entry: us-west | dedicated-large | 8 | 220 | 120ms/420ms | =8*220*60 | = (col - proj)/col | tight

4) Projected Demand (A122..F200)
   Calculated from Pilot Inputs + Traffic Phases.
   - Projected requests/min = cohort_active_users * requests_per_user_per_minute * traffic_percentage
   - Projected tokens/min = Projected requests/min * avg_tokens_per_request
   - Note: requests_per_user_per_minute derived from telemetry baseline or UX estimates (use conservative = 95th percentile).

5) SLO Burn & Escalation Matrix (A202..L270)
   Columns: Time window | Total requests | Errors | Error rate | SLO target | Rolling burn | Burn rate trend | Escalation action
   Key formulas (pseudocode to copy into sheet):
   - Error rate = Errors / Total requests
   - Rolling burn = (Error rate - SLO target) * Total requests / SLO target
   - Escalation action = IF(Rolling burn>1000, "pause-cohort & page-oncall", IF(Rolling burn>250, "reduce-traffic 50% & notify PM", "monitor"))

6) Contingency Checklist (A272..A320) - boolean checkboxes expected in sheet UI
   - Toggle: auto-fallback enabled (owner: eng-release)
   - Action: reduce cohort traffic to X% (owner & script)
   - Action: route to smaller model variant (e.g. redwood-2.1-4bit)
   - Action: increase caching TTL on common prompt prefixes
   - Action: open incident channel (#pilot-surge) and assign incident lead
   - Action: enable read-only degradation (if applicable)

7) Cost delta & Unit economics (A322..H380)
   Metrics: incremental $/min, $/1000 tokens, expected cost delta vs baseline, cost cap threshold.
   Sample formula: incremental $/min = (Projected tokens/min * $per_token_variant) - baseline $/min

8) Signoffs & Approval log (A382..A420)
   - Required signoffs: Eng Release, SRE, Product, Legal (if data is new PII path), Security (if private deploy)
   - Each row: role | name | date signed | notes | link to approval PR

Notes, tips and gotchas:
- Use 95th percentile for latency budgeting in first 3 phases; switch to p50 for steady state.
- When estimating QPS per user, use telemetry tag "pilot_estimate" to track cohort events separately.
- Prefer pre-warm (KV cache) for common prefixes before increasing traffic past 20%.
- If Dedicated pool is used, consider temporary burst allocation (Jira: INFRA-1009) rather than permanent scaling.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Who will own the automated rollback playbook implementation? (Assign: eng-release or platform-engineering?)
- Confirm $per_token for redwood-2.1-4bit for cost delta calc (Finance pricing table link needed).
- Decision: default allowlist for pilot vs opt-in? (impacts adoption signal modeling)

Relevant links & dashboards:
- Console -> Deployment -> Pilot metrics (link: confluence.redwood/display/PDX/Pilot+Dash)
- SRE dashboard (Grafana): /d/pilot-surge/rate-and-latency
- Incident runbook: confluence.redwood/display/OPS/Pilot+Surge+Runbook

Short checklist for go/no-go at each phase end (copy into phase notes):
- Telemetry steady for 30 minutes (p95 latency within target)
- Error rate <= SLO target for 15 minutes
- Cost delta within cap for phase
- No critical alerts in rate/latency dashboards

Change log (history):
- 2024-11-12: Initial draft (Marina O.)
- 2024-12-05: Added SLO burn formulas and escalation matrix (K. Patel)
- 2025-01-18: Integrated Dedicated burst strategy notes (E. Rivers)
- 2025-02-27: Reviewed with SRE; adjusted headroom thresholds and contingency steps

summary: A planning sheet to model pilot surges: capacity vs demand, SLO burn, cost delta, and a concrete contingency checklist for phased rollouts. Designed for product-ops + SRE + eng-release signoffs.
